spec_match.rationale: Every route to a FencedFrameConfig is actually called with plausible arguments and the verbatim refusal printed, and the attach-and-measure comparison reads the element's real cost (box, frame slot, contentWindow, config) against an iframe.

interactive.rationale: Check-every-route, attach fencedframe, attach iframe and clear all perform live operations and repopulate measured tables; nothing is a lookup.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises 'call every route for real and count how many hand one back' plus the attach-and-measure comparison, which is exactly the page.

edge_cases.rationale: Both worlds are first-class: on this pre-removal build the verdict correctly reads '5 of 5 routes still exist and every one refused', and the prose explicitly explains why the present-but-refusing result is the weaker one and what a post-removal browser will report instead.

references.rationale: The feature index (one folder up, linked by the crumb) carries https://chromestatus.com/feature/6366274495053824, the WICG spec and the intent thread; the page itself is reference-dense in prose. Note the chromestatus link lives on the feature index rather than this concept page.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite runs 4/4 on this browser and its assertions (createElement truthiness trap, HTMLUnknownElement end state, interface/config agreement, illegal constructor) are two-sided contracts that stay true across the removal.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP — a genuinely pre-removal build with the surface enabled: all 5 routes present and refusing (https-seller TypeError, selectURL worklet error, deprecatedReplaceInURN undefined, illegal constructor, config-assignment TypeError); attached fencedframe measured 260x90, window.length 0→0, contentWindow undefined, config null, versus iframe 260x90, 0→1, [object Window]; console clean, no exceptions; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Namespaced console logging is thorough and nothing throws, but unlike the rest of v155 this feature's pages do not load /public/demo-telemetry.js, so no showcaseTelemetry events reach the KV triage pipeline.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, secondary buttons override background and color, explicit focus-visible outlines, tables in .scroller wrappers.

accessibility.rationale: role=status aria-live verdict, captioned scoped tables, titled frames, 44px buttons with visible focus, and the slot is aria-live.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; wide tables scroll inside their own containers and the mobile screenshot is clean.

openQuestions.title: Add the chromestatus link to this concept page's own footer/see-also
openQuestions.detail: Invariant #3 (every page includes the chromestatus.com/feature/<id> link, used by the slug-recovery script) is satisfied by the feature index but not by this concept page, which has no see-also block — unusual for the corpus, where concept pages normally repeat the link. A small see-also section matching the sibling features' pattern would restore the self-heal property per page.

openQuestions.title: Wire this feature's pages into demo telemetry
openQuestions.detail: The other six v155 features load /public/demo-telemetry.js and emit showcaseTelemetry.assert events; this feature's three concept pages log to console only, so the weekly telemetry triage cannot see real-visitor errors on them. Adding the script tag and one assert per action would bring them in line.

summary: A rigorous removal demo whose pre-removal world this environment actually provides: on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) all five config routes exist and all five refused for the exact reasons the page predicts, and the attach-and-measure table showed the element's zero-frame-slot, null-config emptiness against a live iframe — verified over CDP at http://localhost:3000/v155/remove-fencedframe-element-and-window-fence-apis/the-frame-that-cannot-navigate/ with clean console and no overflow on either class. Feature /conformance/ route ran 4 pass / 0 fail. Remaining gaps are plumbing: no per-page chromestatus link and no demo-telemetry hookup.
